newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Controversial director to leave Vienna theatre.
newsitem.headline: Controversial director to leave Vienna theatre.

text.p: Claus Peymann, controversial director of Vienna's historic Burgtheater, has said he will leave his post in two years, saying criticism of his work and the theatre was unbearable.

Peymann, from Bremen in Germany, has been director of the prestigious former court theatre since 1986. In a letter faxed to Austrian chancellor Viktor Klima last week he said he would not renew his contract when it ran out in 1999.
"I found the debate about my work, the actors and the Burgtheater unbearable and I am not prepared to ignore this 'smear campaign'," he said on state radio.

Peymann has ruffled many Austrian feathers through his avant-garde direction and by putting on plays that dealt with the nation's murky wartime past, notably "Heldenplatz" or "Hero Square" by the late Austrian playwright Thomas Bernhard.
